crop.notes: The Allen notice under 'Sporting Notes', between a baseball line and an unrelated story 'DUE TO THE TORNADO' (C. H. Sawyer Manufacturing Company). Only the Allen notice is about him.

ocr.notes: The Allen notice is readable ('puetiist' for 'pugilist'); the Sawyer story is mostly right.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat's Sporting Notes carried a notice for Tom Allen, "retired champion pugilist of the world," at 619 Market Street, offering a free concert every evening with only the best singers.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Wednesday Morning, June 17, 1896', page 7. The item is at the top of the far-right column.

facts.fact: Allen advertised his place at 619 Market Street, St. Louis, as the 'retired champion pugilist of the world', with a free concert every evening

notes: Paid notice in the Sporting Notes column; the same notice ran on several days in June 1896. Focus is primary for the notice itself, though it is only three lines.
